data.title: lofsite sandbox fan-out breaks on spatial dialects before DB-4 M5's emit() lands

data.body: Discovered while implementing DB-3. lofsite/rendering.py's render_all_dialects() catches (ValueError, TypeError) from get_renderer() construction to skip parameterised mechanisms, but does not catch NotImplementedError from renderer.render(). Any spatial ComposedRenderer dialect (all 8 of DB-3's archetypes: trees, blocks, graph, map, map-centred, rooms, rna_arc, paths_lite) constructs fine but raises NotImplementedError at pipeline/emit.py's spatial branch (by design, per that module's own docstring, until DB-4 M5 pins a rasteriser). If DB-3's archetypes were fully registered into the renderer registry (register_renderer/-T resolution), 5 of tests/test_lofsite.py's tests fail this way. Worked around for now: DB-3's archetypes/__init__.py populates ARCHETYPE_REGISTRY and DIALECT_SPECS but deliberately withholds the register_renderer step, so -T renderer=<dialect_id> does not yet resolve for these 8 dialects. Fix needs either (a) DB-4 M5 landing real spatial emit(), or (b) lofsite/rendering.py's render_all_dialects catching NotImplementedError alongside (ValueError, TypeError) and reporting it in .skipped, whichever lands first -- then DB-3's registration can be un-deferred (one-line change, see lofbench/renderers/archetypes/__init__.py's _register_named_dialect_when_ready). Needs scoping: which of DB-4/DB-6 owns the fix, and whether lofsite should treat 'constructs but errors on render' as skip-and-report or as a hard failure.

data.reason: Plan is DB-3's reviewer-specified two-liner: spatial emit lands in DB-4 M5-rest, lofsite guard lands in DB-6 phase 2; DB-9 closes when both merge

data.body: Resolved by two merged, reviewed changes: DB-4 M5-rest implemented spatial emit (SVG to PNG data URI, cairosvg pinned) and DB-6 phase 2 added the fan-out guard (render-time NotImplementedError skip plus PNG image panels). Reviewed within the DB-4c and DB-6b reviews; lofsite tests green with the real registry (25 panels render, only the parameterised composed mechanism skips).
